newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares gain, seen firming.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares gain, seen firming.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 0.3 percent in a technical rebound on Tuesday and traders said they expected further moderate gains before the end of the week.
"According to latest news Slovenia's chances to join NATO in the first round of its expansion have increased. That may be sufficient to push the index up slightly this week," a trader said.
Membership of NATO and the EU was expected to encourage foreign investors to buy Slovenian securities as the country's credit rating was likely to improve in the event of membership, he added.
Market participants said future direction would hinge upon whether parliament ratified an agreement with the European Union within the next two weeks.

"When the agreement is ratified shares may jump 10 percent in a matter of days, but if parliament fails to do so shares could fall by 10 to 30 percent," said Goran Brankovic, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska Banka.
The blue-chip index firmed 0.3 percent to 1,318.89.

Petrol company Petrol was the most actively traded share, up 0.76 percent to 17,330 tolars on volume of 1,848 shares. Traders said Petrol could rise to 18,000 tolars in the short-term due to its good business results and favourable prospects.

Overall eleven shares rose, six fell, one was unchanged and ten were untraded. Turnover jumped to 80.3 million tolars from 25 million. On Monday the bourse was closed for two hours on Monday morning due to techinical problems.

Brokerage Dadas was the top gainer, up 5.34 percent to 7,300 on volume of 50 shares and traders said although Dadas had some growth potential due to its plan to expand its franchising business the share remained fairly illiquid.

Construction company GPG was the leading decliner, closing 5.4 percent lower at 4,730 on volume of 300 shares. Brokers said the move was made in a single transaction and added GPG may have already bottomed out.
"In the medium-term GPG could rise to some 8,000 tolars as its price is very cheap when one looks at its business results," one said.
